chapter: Europe and the Black and Blue years
title: Copying the old lifestyle: a young singer imitating Billie Holiday's drinking
summary: Dance says Hamilton copied the 1930s lifestyle. Humes tells a young woman singer who fell off a bar stool and said 'Billie Holiday drank' that she need not pattern herself on Billie; Benny Goodman gave that singer her start.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well you know, I think part of the trouble with Scotty too, is his background. I mean, the reason that voice is so wonderful is that he fell in love with the 1930s, didn't he, and listen to all his records, and he worshipped all those musicians and then he copied their life style, you know, to some extent he copied their life style.
But you can have a life style of your own.
Yeah, right.
You know, a lot of them feel like a little friend of his come telling me. She get up there and she drank and fell off the bar stool and . . .

And I said, 'you got so much in front of you. Why would you want to do something like this'? "Everybody drinks". I said, "but this is what's going to happen to you, you're going to be pissy everytime somebody says, 'hello'. Well, you're backing out, sweetheart." "Well, Billie Holiday drank." I said, "well you see where Billie is, is that what you're trying to do? I mean you can just go on and kill yourself. You don't have to be trying to pattern after Billie". So that was her song.
